text:
maya.k: Heads-up — forecasting a 22% mismatch next 72h between hosted API embed demand and our committed GPU pool in us-west-2. Spike tied to a new customer that started bulk embedding + nighttime batch windows. Need immediate hedging options.

samir: Ugh. Do we know if this is steady tail or a few big batches? Can we throttle/queue them?

maya.k: It's bursty but recurring nightly for the next week per customer schedule. They hit 10k slots in a 2h window last night.

igor: Can we route some requests to eu-west-1 spare capacity? Latency for embeddings is softer but some customers are latency-sensitive.

leah: For that customer specifically we have a contract SLO of 200ms p95, so can't move all traffic. Maybe partial routing + degrade model size?

maya.k: Options I'm thinking: 1) temporarily buy short-term reserved instances / convert on-demand credits 2) shift lower-priority batches to off-peak buckets 3) use quantized smaller embed model for that renter 4) filing a credit request with cloud?

samir: 1 and 2 sound best immediate. Finance needs an estimate for short-term commit size. Also check if billing shows any over-provisioned reserved SKUs that can be swapped.

finance-bot: Quick lookup: last 30d reserved GPU SKUs with >80% idle: [g4dn.xlarge, p3.2xlarge] — see billing tag "team:research". If we can repurpose, might avoid new spend.

leah: Re-tagging those to "capacity-hedge" will require a ticket and change freeze? Who owns them?

nina: I can open the ticket. But we need confirmation that moving will not break Dedicated customers.

maya.k: I ran a quick query:
```
SELECT region, sku, SUM(allocated_hours) - SUM(used_hours) as idle_hours
FROM billing.gpu_usage
WHERE month = CURRENT_DATE()
GROUP BY region, sku
ORDER BY idle_hours DESC
```
Results show ~1.6k idle GPU-hours in us-east-1 and ~900 in eu-west-1 that could be shifted with minimal impact.

igor: Nice. How fast can we pattern-route embedding requests between regions? We have smart routing but need policy update and possibly TTL bump. Could be minutes.

samir: If we do policy + short conversion of on-demand to reserved credits, what's the cost delta? Finance-bot, can you run a quick compare for a 72h hedge of 50 GPUs in us-west-2?

finance-bot: Estimate rough numbers: 50 x p4d for 72h on-demand ~= $460k. 72h on a short-term committed (if provider permits hour-based convertible) ~= $320k. Net savings ~30%. (I can generate detailed invoice on demand).

leah: 460k for 3d seems high — are we sure SKU choice? Could use a quantized model on g5/rtx to reduce hours.

maya.k: Good point. We can pack embeddings more efficiently; kernel optimizations cut per-token GPU time by ~18% for the smaller model. That may reduce required GPU count to ~40.

samir: So 40 x p4d 72h on-demand ~ 368k vs committed 256k. Still big but doable if we spread across finance windows. Also don't forget marketplace credits.

igor: What about immediate technical mitigations: prefix caching, batching window increase from 5ms to 25ms, and per-tenant rate smoothing? Those could reduce peak by ~25% without customer changes.

maya.k: Let's implement batching window increase for embed route and a temporary heuristic: if tenant == heavy-embed-cust then use model-small-emb unless p95 under 220ms. I'll open a rollout canary.

deploy-bot: Canary started for config change: route: /embed -> batching_ms: 25, model_hint: model-small-emb (canary nodes only). Canary id: canary-2024-174778. Rolling 10% -> 50% -> 100% if no errors.

samir: Great. Parallel path: nina, open ticket for re-tagging idle reserved SKUs and assign to ops. Finance will stand up short-term purchase if necessary.

nina: Ticket created: INF-4721 — re-tag idle GPS SKUs + risk assessment. Assigned to @igor.

igor: I'll run risk checks and get back in 30m. Also will simulate routing shift to eu-west-1 in staging.

maya.k: Also noticed a billing oddity: there were two overlapping committed reservations in us-west-2 for the same SKU last billing cycle. Can someone triage with cloud account team? Might be double-charged.

finance-bot: Flagged to cloud rep — case CR-9812 opened. Attachments: invoice diff, reservation ids.

leah: If double-charged we might get credit that covers part of the hedge cost. Good catch.

samir: To summarize action items: 1) ops: implement batching window + model hint canary (maya/igor) 2) nina: ticket INF-4721 for re-tagging 3) finance: prepare short-term commit approval + monitor CR-9812 4) deploy-bot: watch canary metrics (latency, errors, token throughput).

maya.k: I'll run a 4h forecast after the canary to see if peak needs purchases. Will post back with numbers. :thumbsup:

igor: On it. If we still need buys after soft mitigations, prefer convertible short-term commit for cheapest unit economics.

deploy-bot: Canary at 50% without regressions after 18m. p95 latency for canary group: 210ms. Errors: 0.1% (expected minor).

maya.k: Good signal. Waiting for 4h forecast update.

samir: Thanks everyone. Keep this thread updated — if finance approves, we should execute within the next 6h to secure capacity pricing. :eyes:
